items.title: Label rename in-app
items.originalProblemStatement: Users cannot rename project labels from within the PMO app. Labels are auto-created by Planner with default color-based names (Pink, Red, Yellow, etc.) and can only be renamed by opening Planner directly. This forces users out of the PMO app for a routine label management action.
items.proposedSolutionApproach: Wire the existing useRenameLabel hook and PSS PssUpdateV1 wrapper (renameLabel in schedulingClient.ts) into the label picker UI in TaskDetailPanel. Add an inline edit or pencil-icon trigger next to each label in the "+ Add label" dropdown that allows the user to set msdyn_projectlabeltext via PSS update. The PSS wrapper and mutation hook are already built and exported â€” only the UI binding is missing.
architecturalConsiderations: PSS PssUpdateV1 on msdyn_projectlabel is the only supported write path for label rename (confirmed by MS docs: Labels support Update only, not Create or Delete)
useRenameLabel hook already exists in hooks/useProjectLabels.ts with optimistic cache update
renameLabel function already exists in lib/schedulingClient.ts
msdyn_projectlabeltext is the field to update
Labels are project-scoped (auto-created per project, 25 slots)

items.title: Label chips on Kanban board task cards
items.originalProblemStatement: Labels assigned to a task are only visible when the task detail panel is open. The Kanban board cards (TaskRow) do not display any label indicators, making it impossible to see task categorization at a glance in the board view. Planner shows colored label dots on each card.
items.proposedSolutionApproach: Thread label data from TaskWorkspace through BucketSection â†’ TaskRowTree â†’ TaskRow via a new taskLabelMap prop (same pattern as assignmentMap and dependencyMap). In TaskRow, render small colored dots or abbreviated label chips below the task title using the label color palette already defined in TaskDetailPanel.

The label data (projectLabels + allTaskLabels) is already fetched in TaskDetailPanel hooks â€” needs to be lifted to TaskWorkspace level
useProjectLabels and useProjectTaskLabels hooks would need to be called in TaskWorkspace or ProjectDetailPage and passed down
Color mapping (PLANNER_NAMES and PALETTE arrays) should be extracted to a shared constant instead of duplicated
Performance: allTaskLabels query fetches all task-to-label junctions with $top: 5000 â€” acceptable for current project sizes

items.title: Timeline / Gantt view for task scheduling visualization
items.defermentRationale: Deferred from Planner Task Parity Sprint. Large effort requiring Gantt library selection and significant UI engineering. Data layer is fully available â€” deferral is purely about rendering complexity and library validation.
items.originalProblemStatement: The PMO app has no timeline or Gantt view. Users must open Planner to see the Schedule view for visualizing task dates, durations, and dependencies on a timeline. All the underlying data (msdyn_scheduledstart, msdyn_scheduledend, msdyn_projecttaskdependency) already exists and is fetched in TaskWorkspace â€” only the rendering component is missing.
items.proposedSolutionApproach: Add a "Timeline" tab to TaskWorkspace alongside Board and List tabs. Use a Gantt rendering library (frappe-gantt for MIT license and small SVG-based bundle, or dhtmlx-gantt for richer features, or custom SVG renderer for full control). Map ProjectTask[] + ProjectTaskDependency[] to the library's row/link format. Click on a bar opens TaskDetailPanel. Optional interactive drag-to-resize would update dates via PSS PssUpdateV1.
architecturalConsiderations: Must work within the Power Apps Code App host (Vite build, no native DOM shell)
Bundle size impact of Gantt library must be evaluated (frappe-gantt ~15KB gzipped, dhtmlx-gantt ~200KB+)
All required data is already in memory in TaskWorkspace (tasks with dates, dependencies with link types)
Interactive edits (drag to change dates) require PSS PssUpdateV1 calls with PSS_DELAY.TASK_UPDATE (20s) persistence lag â€” complex optimistic update pattern needed
WBS hierarchy should be reflected in the Gantt (indented rows for child tasks under summary parents)
The existing view switcher (Board/List) provides the exact UI pattern for adding a third tab

items.title: Charts panel for task-level summary signals
items.originalProblemStatement: The PMO app has no task-level charts or summary signals in the task workspace. Portfolio-level analytics exist on the Analytics pages, but the Tasks tab has no visual summary of task status distribution, completion rates by bucket, or priority breakdown. Planner provides a Charts view with these signals.
items.proposedSolutionApproach: Add a "Charts" tab to TaskWorkspace showing computed visualizations from the existing in-memory task data. Charts include: task completion donut (not started / in progress / complete), tasks by bucket bar chart, tasks by priority bar chart, overdue count callout, effort distribution. Use recharts (likely already in ecosystem) or lightweight SVG components.

items.title: Workload / People view for resource capacity visualization

items.proposedSolutionApproach: Add a "People" tab to TaskWorkspace that groups resource assignments by team member. For each member, show: assigned tasks list, total effort hours (sum of msdyn_effort from assigned tasks), effort completed, completion rate. Optionally show a visual capacity bar if workload data is available from msdyn_resourceassignment.msdyn_plannedwork.

items.title: Drag-and-drop task cards between Kanban buckets
items.defermentRationale: Deferred from Planner Task Parity Sprint. PSS write path is confirmed but optimistic UI with 20s persistence lag and WBS parent-child drag semantics need careful design. Needs DnD library integration.
items.originalProblemStatement: Tasks cannot be moved between buckets by dragging cards on the Kanban board. Users must use the task detail panel or Planner to change a task's bucket assignment. This is a core Kanban interaction that Planner supports natively.
items.proposedSolutionApproach: Integrate a DnD library (dnd-kit recommended â€” React-first, accessible, small bundle) to enable dragging TaskRow cards between BucketSection columns. Each drop triggers a PSS PssUpdateV1 updating msdyn_projectbucket@odata.bind on the task. The optimistic update pattern holds the new bucket assignment in the TanStack Query cache until the re-fetch settles after PSS_DELAY.TASK_UPDATE.
architecturalConsiderations: PSS write path for bucket reassignment is confirmed working (msdyn_projectbucket@odata.bind in PssUpdateV1)
The 20s PSS persistence lag (PSS_DELAY.TASK_UPDATE) means the optimistic update must hold the new bucket assignment in memory for an extended period
dnd-kit is React-first, accessible, and has a small bundle (~10KB gzipped)
WBS hierarchy complicates drag behavior â€” should a parent task drag bring its children? Should children be draggable independently?
Multiple rapid drags before persistence could cause state inconsistencies

dependenciesOrPrerequisites.description: PSS PssUpdateV1 bucket reassignment works
Optimistic update pattern for task mutations exists
DnD library selection and integration

knownRisksOrTradeoffs.mitigation: Show a subtle "syncing" indicator on recently-dropped cards; prevent re-dragging until persistence confirms

knownRisksOrTradeoffs.description: WBS parent-child drag semantics are complex

supportingResearchOrDesignNotes.title: DnD library recommendation
supportingResearchOrDesignNotes.content: The Planner Task Parity Sprint Plan classified this as "Feasible with additional work and validation" with medium effort. PSS write path for bucket reassignment is confirmed (msdyn_projectbucket@odata.bind). The plan recommended dnd-kit (React-first, accessible, small bundle). The main concern is optimistic UI behavior with the 20s persistence lag â€” the plan says "the optimistic update must hold the new bucket assignment in memory until the query invalidation settles." The existing optimistic update pattern in useUpdateProjectTask provides the template for this, but drag-and-drop introduces rapid successive mutations that need to be serialized.

items.implementationNotes: Implemented using HTML5 native Drag and Drop API — zero external dependencies (no dnd-kit or react-beautiful-dnd). items.title: Additional dependency link types (FF/SS/SF) beyond Finish-to-Start
items.defermentRationale: Deferred from Planner Task Parity Sprint. Small effort â€” all infrastructure is complete. Deprioritized in favor of higher-impact parity features.
items.originalProblemStatement: The PMO app only supports Finish-to-Start (FS) dependencies. The msdyn_projecttaskdependency entity supports four link types via msdyn_linktype (0=FS, 1=FF, 2=SS, 3=SF), and Planner allows creating all four types. The current dependency manager dialog hardcodes msdyn_linktype: 0 (FS) for all new dependencies and does not display the link type for existing ones.
items.proposedSolutionApproach: Add a link type selector (dropdown with FS/FF/SS/SF options) to the dependency creation flow in the Dependency Manager dialog and the TaskDetailPanel predecessors section. Display the link type abbreviation next to each predecessor in the UI. Update createProjectTaskDependency in schedulingClient.ts to accept a linkType parameter instead of hardcoding 0.
architecturalConsiderations: msdyn_linktype field already exists in ProjectTaskDependency model (0=FS, 1=FF, 2=SS, 3=SF)
The dependency read API already fetches msdyn_linktype
Only the UI and the create function need changes â€” no new API calls or entity registration
The PSS PssCreateV1 for dependencies already works; just need to pass a different msdyn_linktype value

dependenciesOrPrerequisites.description: msdyn_projecttaskdependency model includes msdyn_linktype
Dependency CRUD via PSS works (FS type)

supportingResearchOrDesignNotes.title: Implementation simplicity
supportingResearchOrDesignNotes.content: The Planner Task Parity Sprint Plan noted: "Other link types (FS/FF/SS/SF) are supported by the entity but only FS is exposed in UI." The createProjectTaskDependency function in schedulingClient.ts currently hardcodes msdyn_linktype: 0 (Finish-to-Start). items.title: Fix progress onTasksInvalidate using hardcoded 24s instead of PSS_DELAY.TASK_UPDATE
items.defermentRationale: Originally deferred as a low-priority bug fix from the Planner Task Parity Sprint. Implemented in the same session after the tiered delay system was built.
items.originalProblemStatement: The handleProgressSet and handleProgressToggle functions in TaskDetailPanel use a hardcoded setTimeout(onTasksInvalidate, 24_000) instead of the tiered PSS_DELAY.TASK_UPDATE constant (20s). This is inconsistent with the benchmark-based tiered delay system and results in a 4-second unnecessary wait for progress re-fetch.
items.proposedSolutionApproach: Replace setTimeout(onTasksInvalidate, 24_000) with setTimeout(onTasksInvalidate, PSS_DELAY.TASK_UPDATE) in both handleProgressSet and handleProgressToggle in TaskDetailPanel.tsx. Import PSS_DELAY from useProjectTaskMutations.
architecturalConsiderations: PSS_DELAY is already imported in many hooks; adding the import to TaskDetailPanel is trivial
The updateTaskProgress function in schedulingClient.ts does not use the delay constants (it's a fire-and-forget PSS call) â€” the delay is managed by the caller in the component

knownRisksOrTradeoffs.description: None â€” this is a one-line constant replacement

supportingResearchOrDesignNotes.title: Benchmark reference
supportingResearchOrDesignNotes.content: The tiered delay system was implemented based on official Microsoft API performance benchmarks (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/project-operations/project-management/project-schedule-api-performance). PSS_DELAY.TASK_UPDATE = 20_000ms (P90 18.72s + buffer). The hardcoded 24_000ms in TaskDetailPanel predates the tiered system and was never updated. Both handleProgressSet and handleProgressToggle call setTimeout(onTasksInvalidate, 24_000) after a successful updateTaskProgress call.

items.title: SPA navigation state loss on browser refresh
items.defermentRationale: Deferred from Planner Task Parity Sprint. Cross-cutting architecture change that affects every page and navigation action. Requires investigation of Power Apps Code App host constraints on URL manipulation before an implementation approach can be selected.
items.originalProblemStatement: When the user refreshes the browser, the app always returns to the home screen instead of the page they were on. The browser URL does not change as the user navigates within the app (no URL-based routing), so there is no way to bookmark or deep-link to a specific project, tab, or task. The user flagged this as a holistic issue to address separately from the task parity sprint.
items.proposedSolutionApproach: Implement URL-based routing using React Router (or the app's existing routing mechanism if one exists). Map navigation state to URL paths/query parameters so that browser refresh, back/forward, and bookmarking work correctly. Key routes: /projects, /projects/:id, /projects/:id/tasks, /programs, /programs/:id, /analytics/*, /dashboard.
architecturalConsiderations: The Power Apps Code App host may impose constraints on URL manipulation (pushState, hash routing)
The existing app navigation likely uses React state to switch between pages â€” need to audit the current routing mechanism
URL-based routing would require updating all navigation triggers (sidebar links, breadcrumbs, card clicks) to use router navigation instead of state changes
Deep linking to specific tasks (opening the TaskDetailPanel for a specific task via URL) would be a significant UX improvement
This is a cross-cutting change that affects the entire app navigation architecture

items.originalProblemStatement: No automated PR-gated validation exists for the PMO CFR Solution repository. All validation (lint, type-check, build, test) is manual. This creates risk of broken merges and removes a safety net for autopilot agent-driven implementation.
items.proposedSolutionApproach: Create a GitHub Actions workflow at .github/workflows/pr-validation.yml that runs on PRs targeting main. The workflow executes: npm ci, npx tsc -b --noEmit, npm run build, npm test. Fail-fast on any step failure. Workflow blocks merge on failure via branch protection rules.
architecturalConsiderations: Requires GitHub Actions runners configured for the CVS Health GitHub Enterprise instance
Node.js LTS 20+ runner image required (matches local dev environment)
Workflow must run in the app/ subdirectory context (cd app before npm commands)
Branch protection rules on main must be updated to require the workflow status check
The mandatory validation sequence is defined in power-apps-code-app-operating-standard.md: lint, type-check, build, test

supportingResearchOrDesignNotes.title: Workflow specification
supportingResearchOrDesignNotes.content: The workflow should use a standard Node.js GitHub Actions setup: actions/checkout@v4, actions/setup-node@v4 with node-version 20, then sequential steps: npm ci (in app/), npx tsc -b --noEmit, npm run build, npm test. items.originalProblemStatement: The current admin intake workflow configuration exposes raw JSON and OData internals — conversion rules as a JSON textarea, field logical names like pmo_name and _pmo_targetteam_value, and OData bind syntax like pmo_PrimaryTeam@odata.bind. Administrators are not developers. They should never see field logical names, JSON, or OData syntax. The approver group input is a raw AAD group GUID text field with no lookup capability. No default workflow auto-creation exists, requiring manual configuration before any intake is possible.
items.proposedSolutionApproach: Three changes: (1) Replace conversion rules JSON textarea with a visual two-column field mapper using dropdowns with human-readable labels — the component serializes to/from JSON internally. Add CONVERSION_FIELD_OPTIONS constant mapping allowed intake/project fields to labels with pre-determined transform types. (2) Replace approver group GUID text input with a dropdown populated from Dataverse team records (teamtype eq 2 for AAD group teams). Admin selects by name, component stores azureactivedirectoryobjectid. (3) Add Quick Setup button in IntakeWorkflowConfigSection that seeds a standard 3-stage workflow when no workflows exist.
architecturalConsiderations: The visual mapper must serialize to the same ConversionRule[] JSON schema that intakeValidation.ts validates (intakeField, projectField, transform)
Lookup fields always use odata_bind transform, scalar fields always use direct — this is deterministic from the field selection and should not be exposed to the admin
The CONVERSION_FIELD_OPTIONS constant must stay in sync with the ALLOWED_INTAKE_FIELDS_FOR_MAPPING and ALLOWED_PROJECT_FIELDS sets in intakeValidation.ts
The AAD team dropdown reuses the same useTeams pattern from AdminSettingsPage but filters to teamtype eq 2 (AAD group teams)
No schema changes required — this is a UX-only change with no Dataverse impact
